title: Bayes optimal actions, recommendations, and posterior risk
scope: FiniteHorizon.theorem1 is the principal endpoint for any finite collection of N Borel sampling rules and one terminal rule, defined only on the paper's proper Gaussian states, for arbitrary finite K and positive real precisions. Its premise is actual posterior-risk minimization against concrete Borel full-history policies at each state and remaining budget H <= N. It derives the Bellman risk identity, almost-sure EBI-maximizing sampling, and maximal-mean recommendation. Padding the finite rule collection and extending outside positive precisions preserve direct execution and risk. The supporting generic theorems also derive these conclusions from single-state minimization. No Bellman-action premise, rule beyond the finite budget, or optimality at a larger horizon is assumed.

title: Polynomial Gaussian-tail lower bounds exactly characterize the logarithmic gap scale
scope: This is the separately requested corrected statement, not text in the unchanged PDF. For every deterministic d : Nat -> Real with d(T) >= 0, the existence of real c > 0 and p > 0 and a natural T0 such that P[Z_T >= d(T)] >= c*T^(-p) for every T >= T0 is equivalent to Lean IsBigO at infinity of d(T) against T^(-3/2)*sqrt(log T). Z_T has the actual normalized Gaussian law with mean zero and variance T^(-3). The proof includes exact Gaussian standardization, both implication directions, and conversion from an eventual natural-exponent bound to the explicit positive-real-exponent formulation. No monotonicity or further regularity of d is assumed; sufficiently large horizons handle the finite zero/log edge cases. The original Footnote 14 necessity claim remains separately refuted.
